components.name: Horizontal Divider
components.description: A structural separator drawn as a horizontal line used to create visual breaks between content areas, list items, and sections. Stretches to fill its container width with no height footprint.

properties.name: Type
properties.notes: Continuous = solid unbroken line; Dashed = 6px dash / 6px gap; Stylised = linear gradient fade.

properties.name: Colour
properties.notes: Primary=Border/Primary (#262626); Secondary=Border/Secondary (#333333); Tertiary=Border/Tertiary (#4D4D4D); Blured=Border/Primary-30% (#1F1F1F at 30%, adds background blur); Mixed=not tokenised, uses Surface-Secondary-Gradient/Small paint style.

variants.name: Type=Continuous, Colour=Primary
variants.semantic_use: Strongest — high-contrast separators on dark surfaces

variants.name: Type=Continuous, Colour=Secondary
variants.semantic_use: Standard — default for most list rows and section breaks

variants.name: Type=Dashed, Colour=Secondary
variants.semantic_use: Optional/inactive zones, form field separators, boundary states

variants.name: Type=Dashed, Colour=Tertiary
variants.semantic_use: Optional/inactive zones, form field separators, boundary states

variants.name: Type=Continuous, Colour=Blured
variants.example: Border/Primary-30% -> Greys/Grey-900 -> #1F1F1F at 30% opacity, 1px, background blur (frosted surface)

variants.name: Type=Stylised, Colour=Mixed
variants.semantic_use: Editorial sections, marketing surfaces — never functional UI
variants.example: Surface-Secondary-Gradient/Small paint style, linear gradient #1F1F1F -> #262626, 0.5px; reference the paint style by name, not constructed from tokens

rules: Prefer spacing tokens over dividers wherever whitespace alone creates sufficient separation.
Always default to Continuous / Secondary for list rows and section breaks unless context requires otherwise.
Use Dashed only to signal optional, inactive, or boundary states — not as decoration.
Use Blured only on translucent or glass-effect surfaces. Do not use on solid backgrounds.
Use Stylised only on editorial or marketing surfaces — never in functional UI such as lists, forms, or navigation.
Stroke weight is 0.5px (Blured variant is 1px); width 393px stretches to fill container; height 0px (line only).

components.name: Vertical Divider
components.description: A structural separator drawn as a vertical line for inline separation between sibling elements in a horizontal row. No width footprint; container height 24px.

properties.name: Type
properties.notes: Padded = 16px line in 24px container with 4px breathing room top and bottom; Full height = 24px line fills the full container height flush.

properties.name: Colour
properties.notes: Tertiary=Border/Tertiary (#4D4D4D), default subtle inline separation; Secondary=Border/Secondary (#333333), stronger higher-contrast separator.

variants.name: Type=Padded, Colour=Tertiary
variants.semantic_use: Default — subtle inline separation in list rows and action groups
variants.example: Border/Tertiary -> #4D4D4D, line 16px, container 24px, 4px top & bottom padding

variants.name: Type=Padded, Colour=Secondary
variants.example: Border/Secondary -> #333333, line 16px, container 24px, 4px top & bottom padding

variants.name: Type=Full height, Colour=Tertiary
variants.semantic_use: Between equal-height blocks, action rows, tab bar items

variants.name: Type=Full height, Colour=Secondary
variants.semantic_use: Between equal-height blocks, action rows, tab bar items

use_cases.context: Between chips, tags, icon-label pairs, inline items needing visual space
Between equal-height blocks, action rows, tab bar items

rules: Vertical dividers are for inline separation only — between sibling elements in a horizontal row.
Do not use vertical dividers to separate vertically stacked content.
Use Padded between items that need visual breathing room.
Use Full height only when adjacent items share the same height and a flush line is intentional.
Stroke weight is 0.5px; width 0px (line only); container height 24px.

components.name: Base Radio
components.description: The base radio control atom. Used inside a Slot where the parent component controls layout and label.
rules: Use Base only when the control sits inside a Slot — the slot's parent component provides the label and layout.
Indeterminate state is never valid on Radio.
Never mix Radio and Checkbox in the same group.

components.name: Base Checkbox
components.description: The base checkbox control atom. Used inside a Slot where the parent component controls layout and label.

properties.name: Promoted
properties.notes: Applies a highlighted ring or emphasis treatment to draw attention to a specific option (e.g. recommended plan, pre-selected preference, featured option). Disabled always overrides promoted styling.

properties.name: Indeterminate
properties.notes: Partial selection state.

variants.name: Promoted=True / Is disabled=True
variants.semantic_use: Promoted + disabled — uses the same disabled visual as the default (non-promoted) disabled state

rules: Use Base only when the control sits inside a Slot — the slot's parent component provides the label and layout.
There is no separate disabled style for the Promoted variant; disabled always overrides promoted styling.
Indeterminate state is valid on Checkbox.
Never mix Radio and Checkbox in the same group.

components.name: Radio with Text
components.description: A single standalone labelled radio control (not inside a list). Combines a base radio with title and body text and optional leading/trailing slots.

properties.name: Size
properties.notes: Small = dense lists, compact forms; Med = standard forms, settings.

properties.name: Align
properties.notes: Left = radio on left, label on right (default); Right = label on left, radio on right (right-aligned selection rows).

properties.name: Title
properties.notes: Toggles the title text line on/off.

properties.name: Body
properties.notes: Toggles the body/description text line on/off.

properties.name: L-Slot
properties.notes: Toggles the leading (left) slot on/off. Enable to reveal a slot placeholder; place a component inside (Avatar Brand for bank/app logos, Avatar People for contacts, Icon for category indicators).

properties.name: R-Slot
properties.notes: Toggles the trailing (right) slot on/off. Enable for trailing metadata: Badge for counts/status, Icon for disclosure, inline text for pricing/metadata.

properties.name: Title text
properties.notes: Content only — set per design context, not a fixed value.

properties.name: Body text
properties.notes: Content only — set per design context, not a fixed value.

rules: Use 'with Text' only for a single isolated option (not inside a list).
Both L-Slot and R-Slot are off by default; enable and place the correct component inside based on design intent.
Title text / Body text are content properties — populate from design context, no single correct default.

components.name: Checkbox with Text
components.description: A single standalone labelled checkbox control (not inside a list). Component name in Figma is 'Checkox with text' (typo intentional, matches Figma).

properties.name: Size
properties.notes: Small = dense lists, compact forms; Med = standard forms, settings, filters; Large = prominent opt-ins, permissions, terms.

properties.name: Title
properties.notes: Toggles the title text line on/off.

properties.name: Body
properties.notes: Toggles the body/description text line on/off.

properties.name: L-Slot
properties.notes: Toggles the leading (left) slot on/off. Place Avatar (Brand/People), Icon, or thumbnail image inside.

properties.name: R-Slot
properties.notes: Toggles the trailing (right) slot on/off. Place Badge, pricing text, or Icon for info/disclosure inside.

properties.name: Title text
properties.notes: Content only — set per design context.

properties.name: Body text
properties.notes: Content only — set per design context.

use_cases.context: Select a subscription plan with logo

rules: Use 'with Text' only for a single isolated option such as a single 'I agree' checkbox.
Both slots are off by default; enable and place the correct component inside based on design intent.
Title text / Body text are content properties — populate from design context, not from a fixed default.

components.name: Radio with Text (Stack)
components.description: A group of radio options displayed in a vertical list. Default for all final screen designs. Each stack item is a 'Radio with text' instance separated by a built-in Horizontal divider.

properties.name: Count
properties.notes: Plenty renders a scrollable overflow state — use when the count is dynamic or unknown at design time.

rules: Use the Stack in all final screen designs.
Each stack item is a Radio with text instance separated by a Horizontal divider — the divider is built into the stack, do not add dividers manually.
Always use Stack for lists of 1 or more options in final screens.

components.name: Checkbox with Text (Stack)
components.description: A group of checkbox options displayed in a vertical list. Default for all final screen designs. Each stack item is a 'Checkox with text' instance separated by a built-in Horizontal divider.

properties.name: Count
properties.notes: Plenty renders a scrollable overflow state — use when the count is dynamic or unknown at design time.

rules: Use the Stack in all final screen designs.
Each stack item is a Checkox with text instance separated by a Horizontal divider — the divider is built into the stack, do not add dividers manually.
Always use Stack for lists of 1 or more options in final screens.

components.name: Toggle
components.description: A standalone base atom for switching a single setting or preference on or off — an immediate binary action with no confirmation step. There is no Toggle with Text or Toggle Stack variant; place inside a parent layout component when a label is needed.

properties.name: Size
properties.notes: Large = default, settings screens, preference rows; Med = dense rows, inline toggles with limited vertical space.

properties.name: State
properties.notes: Off = inactive, On = active.

properties.name: Promoted
properties.notes: Highlights toggle to grab user attention (adds a highlighted ring). Disabled always overrides promoted.

properties.name: Indeterminate
properties.notes: Loading or unknown state — neither On nor Off. Resolve to definitive On/Off once data is available.

variants.name: Off / Indeterminate=False / Promoted=True / Is disabled=False
variants.semantic_use: Promoted inactive — highlighted to grab attention

variants.name: On / Indeterminate=True / Promoted=False / Is disabled=False
variants.semantic_use: Indeterminate — state is loading or unknown

variants.name: On / Indeterminate=True / Promoted=True / Is disabled=True
variants.semantic_use: Promoted + disabled — falls back to the same disabled visual as non-promoted disabled state

use_cases.context: Live preference that takes effect instantly

rules: Toggle has no Stack or with Text variant — always place it inside a parent layout component when a label is needed.
Promoted=True adds a highlighted ring; when combined with Is disabled=True, promoted styling is suppressed (disabled always overrides promoted).
Indeterminate is used during loading or unknown state; always resolve to a definitive On or Off once data is available.
Use Toggle for immediate/live settings; use Checkbox for selection within a form submitted later or single consent/agreement.
Indeterminate state is valid on both Checkbox and Toggle — never on Radio.
Disabled states are visual only — ensure the disabled logic is also enforced in code.

components.name: Rating Star
components.description: Base atom for a single rating star. Never used directly in screens — it is only the building block for 'rating - star group'.

properties.name: state
properties.notes: full = fully filled, contributes 1.0; half = half-filled, contributes 0.5; empty = unfilled, contributes 0.

variants.name: full
variants.semantic_use: Fully filled star — contributes 1.0 to score

rules: Never place individual rating - star atoms directly in a screen — always use rating - star group.

components.name: Rating Star Group
components.description: A composed star display built from five 'rating - star' atoms. The rating prop drives the combination of full/half/empty stars (0–5 in 0.5 increments). Used for star-based rating scores on product cards, reviews, and listing rows.

properties.name: rating
properties.notes: All 11 values (0–5 in 0.5 steps) are pre-built as variants — always use the variant, never manually arrange individual stars.

rules: Use rating - star group when the full star spread is needed for clarity (product detail pages, review sections).
Rating values are always a number between 0–5 in 0.5 increments — never render a 4.3 or 3.7.
Always use the variant, never manually arrange individual stars.

components.name: Rating Badge
components.description: A self-contained, independent component displaying a compact numeric rating score with its own built-in single star icon and score text. Not derived from rating - star or rating - star group. Used on product cards, thumbnails, and listing rows where a full star group doesn't fit.

properties.name: Type
properties.notes: Translucent = semi-transparent dark over image/media; Green = success fill for high ratings (>= 4.0) on light surfaces; Grey = neutral fill for mid/unrated states; Transparent = no background for inline text/dense rows.

variants.name: Type=Grey
variants.semantic_use: Mid or unrated states on light surfaces

variants.name: Type=Transparent
variants.semantic_use: Inline text contexts, dense data rows

rules: Use Rating badge when horizontal space is constrained and only the score number is needed.
Rating Badge is self-contained with its own built-in single star icon and score text — do not use rating - star group to construct a Rating Badge.

components.name: Autopay Merch
components.description: Renders a merchant brand image inside a standardised card. Each brand is a separate component variant in the 'New' frame. Contains a single Background Image rectangle filled with the brand artwork; there are no text layers inside. Figma component name is 'Autopay Merch componenet' (typo matches Figma).

properties.name: Background Image
properties.notes: The brand artwork fills this rectangle. Map the Figma brand label to the corresponding code asset name; never use the Figma label directly as a file name (casing/spacing differ). Use the 'no-brand-icon' fallback when a brand is not in the list.

rules: Always map the Figma brand label to the corresponding code asset name; never use the Figma label directly as a file name.
Never recolour the brand image — render at full colour only.
Never overlay text directly on the brand image inside the component.
When a brand is not in the list, use the 'No brand icon' fallback variant.
The component does not contain a visible label — the merchant name is always rendered by the parent layout.

components.name: Scrim
components.description: An overlay layer placed between content and backgrounds. This covers the 'Without Blur' section only — the flat/gradient scrim variants. Blur scrims are documented separately.

properties.name: Type
properties.notes: Block = solid fill, full-surface overlay; Top = top->transparent fade down (nav/header overlays); Bottom = transparent->bottom fade up (CTAs above content, tab bar); Bottom sheet = transparent->bottom steep fade for drag handle area.

properties.name: Opacity
properties.notes: 100% = #0D0D0D full, maximum blocking; 70% = #0D0D0D at 70%, standard modal/sheet overlay (most common); 1% = #0D0D0D at 1%, near-invisible tap-capture layer.

properties.name: Use
properties.notes: Toggles scrim layer visibility. False hides the scrim while keeping the node in the layer structure — for states where the scrim conditionally appears. Design articulation only; in code, conditionally render or hide based on state.

rules: Almost all scrims are embedded inside the component they belong to — rarely place a Scrim atom manually. Only place directly when building a custom overlay with no parent component encapsulating it.
Always place Scrim above the content it overlays and below any interactive UI (buttons, close icons).
Use Block for full-page overlays and modals.
Use Top or Bottom gradient variants for partial fades — never stretch a Block scrim and reduce opacity to simulate a gradient.
Use 1% opacity only when an invisible tap-capture layer is required — never for visible overlays.
Never apply additional colour fills or effects on top of the Scrim component.
The Use=False toggle is for design articulation only — in code, conditionally render or hide the scrim based on state.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: The main avatar circle representing people, brands, or system icons in a circular (or square for brand/icon/illustration) container. 72 total variants.

properties.name: Type
properties.notes: People - Initials = circular container with initials text (fallback when no image); People - Image = circular container with photo; Brand = square container with brand logo; Icon = square container with system icon; Illustration = square container with system illustration. (Illustration option spelled 'Illsutration' in Figma.)

properties.name: Fill (for 'Icon' only)
properties.notes: Only applies when Type=Icon. For People and Brand types value is always 'Not icon - People / Brand' and should not be changed. Primary - Highlighted = strong filled bg, high emphasis; Secondary - Highlighted = medium fill; Tertiary - Transparent = no background, low emphasis; Only icon = bare icon, no container fill.

properties.name: Size
properties.notes: 16 = micro (inline mention, dense rows); 28 = small (compact lists, comment rows); 36 = medium (standard list rows, chat); 56 = large (profile headers, contact cards); 64 = XL (prominent profile surfaces); 130 = hero (full profile page, onboarding).

variants.name: Type=People - Initials
variants.semantic_use: When no profile image is available

variants.name: Type=People - Image
variants.semantic_use: When a profile photo is available

variants.name: Type=Icon
variants.example: Square container with a system icon

variants.name: Type=Illustration
variants.example: Square container with a system illustration

rules: Never manually scale an Avatar — always use the nearest available size variant.
Use People - Initials as the fallback when no image is available — never show an empty circle.
Use Brand type only for logos — never for people profiles.
Fill only applies when Type=Icon; for People and Brand types keep 'Not icon - People / Brand'.

components.name: Dot
components.description: A small presence or status indicator attached to an avatar.

properties.name: Colour
properties.notes: Green = online/active; Orange = away/busy (brand); Red = do not disturb/alert; Blue = in a call/focused; Yellow = idle/pending; White = invert, for use on dark avatar rings.

properties.name: Size
properties.notes: 6px pairs with 16px/28px avatars; 8px pairs with 36px/56px; 10px pairs with 64px/130px.

variants.name: Colour=White
variants.semantic_use: Invert — for use on dark avatar rings

rules: Always pair a Dot with the correct avatar size using the size guidance table.
Dot is positioned and sized by the design system — do not reposition it relative to the Avatar circle.

components.name: Flag
components.description: A coloured flag badge marking an avatar with a categorical flag (e.g. premium, verified, new).

properties.name: Type
properties.notes: Orange = brand/promoted; Green = verified/success; Red = alert/flagged; White = invert, light surface contexts.

rules: Always pair a Flag with the correct avatar size using the size guidance tables.
Flag is positioned and sized by the design system — do not reposition it relative to the Avatar circle.

components.name: Fave Icon
components.description: A favourite/bookmark action attached to an avatar (e.g. saved contacts, wishlisted merchants).

properties.name: Size
properties.notes: 20px pairs with 36px avatar; 24px with 56px; 28px with 64px; 32px with 130px.

properties.name: Is active
properties.notes: True = item favourited (filled icon); False = not favourited (outline icon).

variants.name: Is active=False
variants.semantic_use: Item is not favourited — outline icon

rules: Always pair a Fave icon with the correct avatar size using the size guidance table.
Fave icon is positioned and sized by the design system — do not reposition it relative to the Avatar circle.

components.name: Avatar Stack
components.description: An overlapping group of multiple avatars showing a compact group of people (participants, contributors, followers).

properties.name: Count
properties.notes: Number of visible avatars in the overlap (max 3).

properties.name: Type
properties.notes: Logo = brand/app logos; Icon = people/generic icons.

properties.name: More
properties.notes: When True, appends a '+N' overflow indicator after the visible avatars.

rules: Use Avatar stack with More=True when the total count exceeds 3 — do not add more than 3 visible avatars manually.
